description: Golden-vector corpus for .epr-meta evaluator parity — the governance correspondence theorem. Every evaluator (Python PreToolUse hook, Python git-gate, Rust eprfs-meta/epr-cli, any future Codex-side gate) MUST derive these exact outcomes from these cascades. Two runtimes deriving different verdicts from the same manifests is a forked governance plane. Source of truth: this file; runners project it into temp fixture trees. Decision vocabulary: epr:schema:enum:decision (permit|refuse|refer). Severity law: deny > ask > inject; measure/dispatch never block. Ceiling law: ask-class outcomes are REFER (first-class, routed), never a collapsed warn.

vectors.name: no-rule-clean-allow
vectors.law: Silence when no rule fired is clean; nothing to witness.

vectors.name: deny-fires-refuse

manifests..epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: no-new-md
    class: deny
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Deny-class refusal on the deterministic floor.

vectors.name: ask-fires-refer

manifests.notes/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: confirm-notes
    class: ask
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Ask IS the ceiling marker at authoring time — a routed referral, never a collapsed warn and never conflated with deny.

vectors.name: deny-beats-ask-severity

manifests..epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: root-deny
    class: deny
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test
manifests.sub/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: sub-ask
    class: ask
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Severity single-winner: deny > ask. Cascade merges root-first; both fire; deny wins.

vectors.name: inject-only-permits-with-advice

manifests.adv/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: advise-only
    class: inject
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Inject narrows nothing — permit carrying advisory witness.

vectors.name: measure-never-blocks

manifests.m/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: observe-md
    class: measure
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    measure:
      kind: level
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: Observation tier: fires, is witnessed, never blocks.

vectors.name: measure-without-kind-is-malformed

manifests.mk/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: observe-md-no-kind
    class: measure
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    why: test

vectors.law: A measure rule MUST declare measure.kind (level|rate|ratio) — an undeclared kind is how a rate gets compared to a cumulative level (L6, landed 2026-08-11 in 8da9b519c). A rule-integrity failure routes rather than guessing. ADDED 2026-08-12 to pin a MEASURED divergence: the previous form of `measure-never-blocks` carried no kind, and the two evaluators split on it — Python refused the manifest as malformed while Rust accepted it and applied the rule. That is a forked governance plane by this corpus's own definition, and it survived because no gate runs either runner. This vector is expected to PASS in Python and FAIL in Rust until eprfs-meta enforces L6; it is the corpus-level half of the `governance-plane-single-evaluator` habit.

vectors.name: dispatch-permits-and-directs

manifests.d/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: dispatch-review
    class: dispatch
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    require-frontmatter: [title]
    parameters: { dispatch-agent: code-reviewer, dispatch-prompt: "review the governance registry edit" }
    why: test

vectors.law: Dispatch never blocks; it witnesses and directs a background agent. A silently-dropped dispatch verdict is a defect (pre-slice behavior).

vectors.name: unresolvable-validator-refers

manifests.v/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: ghost-validator
    class: deny
    when: { write: "*.md", new: true }
    validator: epr:validator-does-not-exist
    why: test

vectors.law: An unresolvable reference must never soften to inject (the pre-slice soundness inversion) and must not hard-deny at authoring polarity: it routes. Declared runtime-scoped validators (e.g. rust-only) are NOT unresolvable — they are Unavailable-by-declaration and skip without downgrading the rule.

vectors.name: malformed-manifest-refers

manifests.bad/.epr-meta:
rules:
  - id: broken
    class: deny
    when: { write: "*.md" }
    unknown-predicate-key: true

vectors.law: Rule-integrity failure is a ceiling event: the gate cannot know what governance intended, so it routes rather than guessing — unless the write TARGETS the manifest itself (fixing is never blocked).
